basis: Intellectual disability defines the disorder; facial dysmorphism does not establish additional organ damage.
The syndrome is defined by craniosynostosis, congenital heart disease and intellectual disability.
Clostridium tetani infection produces toxin-mediated neuronal dysfunction; muscle spasms do not establish primary muscle damage.
Meningeal tumour within the spinal canal; motor, sensory and sphincter deficits arise from nervous-system compression.
Focal pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction causes excessive insulin secretion and hypoglycemia; common permanent brain injury is not established.
Inherited porphyrin and haem metabolism disorders; no additional damaged organ applies consistently across this broad group.
Metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia with long-bone bowing and metaphyseal abnormalities in all reported patients.
Congenital long-bone bowing defines the disorder; unspecified skin abnormalities lack evidence of common functional damage.
Dilated cardiomyopathy defines the condition; associated myopathy is supported by weakness/Gowers sign in 3/6 and elevated CK in 6/6.
Frontotemporal degeneration and motor-neuron disease; weakness and muscle atrophy reflect denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Intellectual disability defines this neurodevelopmental umbrella; other organ abnormalities vary by subtype.
Epithelial carcinoma involving lymph nodes; lymph nodes have no specified axis, and neither blood-cell origin nor a covered primary site is established.
The definition specifies origin in vulvar apocrine sweat glands, which are skin appendages.
Sulfatide storage destroys nervous-system myelin; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Hearing impairment and cholecystitis are only 5-29%.
Pulmonary fibrosis, platelet storage-pool bleeding and cutaneous albinism define this subgroup; ocular albinism causes visual impairment in nearly all.
Alcohol-induced fibrosis and architectural destruction of the liver; other organ diseases are not intrinsic defining involvement.
Developmental delay 11/11, chronic lung disease 9/10 and camptodactyly 11/11; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic functional damage.
Cerebellar parenchymal disease; the listed subtypes are neurologic ataxia and cerebellar coordination disorders.
Organic acid metabolism defect; developmental disability/dystonia and immunodeficiency each occur in 30-79%. Renal insufficiency is only 5-29%.
Mitochondrial translation defect causes acute liver failure; coagulopathy reflects hepatic synthetic failure, and low IgG alone does not prove immune dysfunction.
An inherited neonatal-infantile epilepsy syndrome; cyanosis and autonomic seizure manifestations do not establish additional organ damage.
Mature teratoma arising within the central nervous system.
Adenocarcinoma arising in the uterine endometrium, a reproductive site outside the axes; estrogen association does not establish endocrine disease.
Vascular insufficiency defines the umbrella; downstream organ injury depends on the affected vascular territory and subtype.
A subtype of primary biliary cholangitis, an autoimmune disease that destroys intrahepatic bile ducts.
